packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — Literal placeholder string "refresh_token" is injected into the parsed data and flows into prisma.credential.key, so a bogus value is later sent to the provider as a real refresh token.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Sync gate here omits the `&& userId` condition that refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 has, so for team credentials (userId null) the real provider is called but the minimum schema is applied, replacing the genuine refresh_token with the placeholder and bricking the credential.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — Spreading parsed data in sync mode overwrites the real refresh_token with the "refresh_token" placeholder and leaves expires_in stale, and line 265 persists it -- every subsequent getToken() sees an expired token and re-refreshes forever.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — key` is the SafeParseReturnType wrapper returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse, so the DB stores `{success:true,data:{...}}` instead of the credential; the next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws and the integration is dead.
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — prisma` is used but never imported in this file, so every SalesforceCalendarService construction throws ReferenceError at runtime.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, a request with no secret header evaluates `undefined !== undefined` as false and the auth check passes, giving unauthenticated write access to any user's credentials.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:93 — refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but a Gaxios `res` locally, so `res?.data` is undefined, `token.access_token` throws TypeError, and the catch swallows it (message !== "invalid_grant") -- refresh silently no-ops forever.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — credential.key is wholesale replaced by the sync endpoint's response body, dropping refresh_token and all other O365 fields from the stored credential.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:98 — Persists only the parsed data, which in sync mode is just access_token, wiping instance_url/id/signature/scope/token_type from credential.key so the next construction builds a jsforce connection with instanceUrl undefined.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Token refresh runs unconditionally on every service instantiation with no expiry check, hammering the Salesforce token endpoint on every availability/booking call.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58 — Falls back to an empty encryption key when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset instead of refusing, so decryption proceeds under a known/degenerate key.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — findFirst with no orderBy or uniqueness: a user with multiple credentials for the same app has an arbitrary one overwritten while the others silently keep stale keys.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — The new webhook route has no HTTP-method guard, so unsupported methods reach body processing instead of returning 405.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — No test covers the relaxed schema branch, whose computed keys fail to preserve provider expiry fields that callers persist.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
